input.quote: If an Obligor is granted a Credit and the application of such Credit to the related Obligor's account results in a shortfall in Collections for the related Collection Period, the Marketing Agent shall deposit, or shall cause the related Originator to deposit, into the Collection Account the related Credit Payment within two (2) Business Days after identification that such Credit was applied to an Obligor account
input.rationale: This transfer and servicing agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction binding the Issuer or the Depositor. Searches for "minimum", "commit to purchase"/"commit", "volume" and "obligated to acquire" return no commitment language, and fees payable by us (the Servicing Fee and related amounts) are consideration for services actually performed rather than a committed spend. The only "shortfall" mechanic on the transaction side, Section 4.3(h) (p0211), runs the other way: it obligates Cellco as Marketing Agent (or the Originator) to deposit Credit Payments when Credits cause a Collections shortfall, which benefits us and is not flagged. Transfers of Additional Receivables (p0034, p0037) are Depositor-to-Issuer, discretionary and conditioned on the Credit Enhancement Test and Pool Composition Tests, so they impose no purchase obligation on us in favour of the counterparty. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; amounts payable only for services rendered), so no redline is warranted.
